prov.heading: Allowance for Credit Losses
prov.text:
OFG measures its ACL based on management’s best estimate of expected credit losses inherent in OFG’s relevant financial assets. Tables 8 through 11 set forth an analysis of activity in the ACL and present selected credit loss statistics for the quarters and nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, and 2025 and as of September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025. In addition, Table 6 sets forth the composition of the loan portfolio.

The decline in the allowance for credit losses reflected, in part, the impact of the sale of two non-performing commercial loans during the period, which reduced specific credit exposure and contributed to improved asset-quality metrics. However, management continued to retain qualitative reserves for areas of uncertainty not fully captured by the quantitative model, including trends in the auto portfolio. As a result, the reserve release reflected an improved risk profile following the non-performing commercial loan sales and other portfolio credit metrics, while qualitative reserves continued to address portfolio-specific risks and uncertainties not fully captured by the quantitative models.

On the retail side, consumer and auto loan portfolios continued to perform well, reporting lower early delinquency and 90 days and over delinquency levels compared to December 31, 2025.

nonint.text: Total Non-Interest Expense was $96.3 million compared to $102.8 million in the second quarter of 2026 and $96.5 million in the third quarter of 2025. The third quarter of 2026 primarily reflected the absence of $5.8 million in business related operational charges in the second quarter of 2026.

nonop.text: Total Interest Expense was $42.2 million compared to $39.9 million in the second quarter of 2026 and $45.4 million in the third quarter of 2025. Interest expense increased $2.3 million sequentially in the third quarter of 2026 primarily reflecting higher average deposit balances at a higher cost and $0.4 million from one additional business day.

pretax.text: Income tax expense for the third quarter of 2026 increased by $5.7 million to $15.2 million from $9.5 million, primarily due to higher income before taxes and fewer favorable discrete items. OFG maintained an ETR lower than the statutory rate for the third quarter of 2026 and 2025 of 21.2% and 15.5%, respectively. The lower ETR is mainly related to exempt income and investments subject to preferential tax treatment under the PR Code. The third quarter of 2025 ETR was further reduced by the cumulative effect of changes in the applicable tax rate recognized during the year.

net.text: With year-over-year increases of 14.7% in EPS, 9.2% in net income and 1.0% in core revenues, third quarter results reflected continued momentum in commercial loan growth, stable credit quality and core deposit balances, disciplined expense management, and healthy profitability. OFG also repurchased $13.5 million of common shares, reinforcing its commitment to creating long-term shareholder value.

Net interest income.heading: Net interest income
Net interest income.text: Net interest income is a function of the difference between rates earned on OFG’s interest-earning assets and rates paid on its interest-bearing liabilities (interest rate spread) and the relative amounts of its interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities (interest rate margin). OFG constantly monitors the composition and re-pricing of its assets and liabilities to maintain its net interest income at adequate levels.

intro.text: OFG is a financial holding company headquartered in San Juan, Puerto Rico. OFG is subject to the provisions of the U.S. Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended, (the “BHC Act”) and accordingly, subject to the supervision and regulation of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (the “Federal Reserve Board”). OFG’s principal subsidiary is Oriental Bank (the “Bank”), a Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (“FDIC”) insured Puerto Rico commercial bank founded as a federal savings and loan in 1964. OFG provides comprehensive banking and financial services and solutions to its clients through the Bank and various other subsidiaries, including commercial, consumer, auto, and mortgage lending, financial planning, insurance sales, investment advisory and security brokerage services, as well as corporate trust services.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
